correctness.rationale: Every path payoff follows from independent Bernoulli turnout and at most one represented ballot. Its distance loss is in [0,Delta q_max]. For Hamiltonian cycles every changed arrow omits vertices, costing at least tau p_min Q/q_max. For any non-Hamiltonian functional graph, transferring from a maximum-abstention-product cycle into another cycle or redirecting a predecessor into a feeder tree increases the position-free payoff by that amount; the strict stated bound dominates the ideology error. Direct rational best-response algebra proves both directions of the three-voter boundary and excludes two-voter nonspanning equilibrium under mutual acceptability. The embedded checker passed 8,027 exact assertions, supporting but not replacing the proof.

value.rationale: In the natural stochastic default-delegation game, one explicit inequality completely classifies the entire pure Nash set for arbitrary finite electorates and heterogeneous turnout, rather than merely guaranteeing some equilibrium or a cycle in every component. It yields the exact equilibrium count and contrasts sharply with an exact three-voter nonspanning-cycle boundary at still mutually acceptable positions. The theorem contributes a structural phase and demonstrates the necessary conceptual gap between ideological acceptability and global cycle stability; general threshold optimality is not asserted.
